Optimal.Notes: TF2 comfortably runs at high/medium settings at a locked 60 fps on the Deck; this is the sweet spot most players will want. Multicore Rendering must be enabled to make full use of the Zen 2 CPU cores.

profiles.Summary: Team Fortress 2 is a lightweight Source Engine game from 2007 that runs exceptionally well on the Steam Deck, easily hitting 60 fps at native resolution with headroom to spare. It is rated Playable on Deck (primarily due to the on-screen keyboard being needed for text chat) and runs natively via Proton with a gold/trending-platinum ProtonDB rating.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the 2007 Source Engine PC requirements (extremely modest by modern standards) and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU, which vastly outclasses TF2's requirements. On first run, check fps in a busy 24-player server — if it dips below your cap, lower Shadow Detail and Effect Detail first.

MaxBattery.Notes: The Source Engine is very light on GPU; a 6 W TDP and 600 MHz GPU clock is more than sufficient to hold a stable 40 fps lock. Disabling VSync and capping via the Deck overlay avoids tearing without the latency of in-game VSync.

KnownIssues: On-screen keyboard may not appear automatically for text chat, requiring manual invocation (Steam button + X).
Some users report occasional stuttering on first launch while shaders compile; subsequent sessions are smooth.
In-game voice chat may require additional audio configuration under Proton.
Microtransaction/item store overlays may occasionally behave unexpectedly under Proton.

MaxPerformance.Notes: TF2's 2007 Source Engine is so lightweight that the Deck can run it fully uncapped at max settings well above 60 fps; battery life is the only real cost. If battery drain is a concern, cap to 60 fps and drop TDP to ~11 W.

Optimal.Notes: TF2's Source engine is well within the Deck's capability at native 800p — 60 fps holds solidly even in crowded 24-player servers. This is the recommended daily-driver profile for most players.

profiles.Summary: Team Fortress 2 is a lightweight Source engine game from 2007 that runs natively well on the Steam Deck, easily hitting high frame rates even at max settings with minimal power draw. ProtonDB reports trend platinum, indicating a smooth out-of-the-box experience with little to no configuration needed.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from TF2's 2007 Source engine requirements (far below Deck capability) and ProtonDB's platinum trend. On first run, check frame rate in a busy 24-player server — it should hold 60+ fps easily, and you can push toward the MaxPerformance profile with confidence.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 6 W TDP and a low render resolution, the Source engine is barely taxed — this profile is ideal for long sessions on the go. Multicore Rendering should always stay enabled on the Deck's 4-core CPU.

KnownIssues: Text chat input may require workarounds with the on-screen keyboard on Deck
Occasional stutters on first-time shader compilation (goes away after initial play session)
Some players report minor audio crackling under Proton; switching to Proton Experimental may help
The in-game store and some overlay elements may not render correctly in certain Proton versions

MaxPerformance.Notes: TF2 at maximum settings is no challenge for the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU — 90 Hz is achievable in most scenarios, though extremely chaotic particle-heavy teamfights may dip into the 70s. Use the OLED's 90 Hz panel to its fullest.
